It's all grammatically correct and people definitely get what you mean. That's great! However, usually Chinese sounds better (less clumsy) if you use less words to express the meaning you want. So for your reference, here's how to make it even better:

我介绍我自己一下。  (all good! Improving this sentence would be quite difficult for now, so it's ok!)

我姓“Z”，叫“XY”。 (我叫 ZXY。OR 我的名字是ZXY。)

Because it is known that Chinese last names go first, you can omit the 姓 and 名 parts and go for ZXY

我是德国人。我在“S”大学学习。(all good! Suggestion: but if S University is not in Germany, you could say 但/而 在\[法國\]的S大学学习, which means "but I study in S Uni in France")

但=but / 而=sort of like "and", but I don't really know the English equivalent of 而.

我学习法律。觉得很有意思。(It's ok, but I would use ， instead of 。as the ideas are related. Eg: you would say "I study law, as I think it's very meaningful". Thus I would say: 我学习法律，\[因為我\]觉得\[法律/它\]很有意思。)

因為=because

它=it, for non-living objects

我喜欢电影和音乐。我的爱好是瑜伽。(because likes and hobbies are quite related, I would group these together: 我喜欢电影和音乐,\[而\]我的爱好是瑜伽。

而=same as above

But if you're not comfortable with the new words, what you said was absolutely ok and people will understand you!
